verdict.rationale: Glama's own hosted Inspector acts as an MCP client. It connects to arbitrary remote Streamable HTTP/SSE MCP servers, handles auth, and executes their tools, so the product does plug in MCP servers and invoke their tools. However, this is a human-driven testing surface, and the Gateway and hosting only proxy tools to external agents. There is no evidence that Glama's own AI (e.g. Glama Chat) consumes plugged-in MCP tools agentically. Missing for 10: evidence that Glama Chat or another Glama AI can attach MCP servers and call their tools autonomously, documentation of a user-facing workflow for using connected tools beyond testing, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools

citations.quote: Glama's hosted inspector connects to remote Streamable HTTP and SSE endpoints so you can inspect available capabilities and test requests interactively
Test any MCP server from your browser. Supports every Model Context Protocol feature, including tools, resources, prompts, tasks, elicitation, sampling, and OAuth 2.1.
Test your local MCP servers with the inspector by exposing them via a public tunnel using mcp-proxy.
